articles.title: In 2019, reality star Eva Marcille bought a Georgia home for $780,000; seven years later, her homeowners association is suing for over $22,000 over alleged unpaid charges and maintenance violations she disputes
articles.summary: Reality television star Eva Marcille is facing a legal dispute with the homeowners association that oversees her Georgia home.
articles.body: Reality television star Eva Marcille is facing a legal dispute with the homeowners association that oversees her Georgia home. The association is seeking more than $22,000 (£16,900) in unpaid fees and fines for alleged property maintenance violations. The lawsuit against the former star of The Real Housewives of Atlanta claims that she failed to meet landscaping rules and left items in public view without approval at her property in Alpharetta, Georgia. According to legal documents obtained by celebrity news outlet TMZ and details reported by Realtor.com, the homeowners association claims Marcille ignored repeated notices about an unkempt lawn, overgrown weeds, broken-down vehicles parked in the driveway, and dustbins left in view. Marcille’s attorney and husband, Michael T. Sterling, confirmed the legal dispute in statements to media outlets. He said he would fight the lawsuit and challenged the association’s right to impose large financial penalties over minor issues involving the appearance of the property.Property details and legal defense strategyMarcille bought the five-bedroom, five-bathroom home in Alpharetta in November 2019 for $780,000 (£598,000). According to property value estimates published by Realtor.com, the 4,700-square-foot home is now worth about $1.35 million (£1.04 million). Representing his wife in court, Sterling made a strong statement about the association’s legal action. “Let me be absolutely clear: Eva Marcille is not going to lose her home over weeds in her lawn or a vehicle parked outside her residence. Period,” Sterling told TMZ in a statement cited by Realtor.com. “I intend to fight this HOA at every turn to protect her property, defend her rights, and hold those responsible accountable,” Sterling continued. “No homeowners association should be allowed to weaponize fines, fees, and liens to intimidate homeowners, particularly over minor violations that should never escalate into a threat against someone's home.” Sterling said the defense would partly rely on recent changes to state law designed to protect property owners from excessive penalties imposed by homeowners associations.Invoking new state homeowner protectionsThe defense plan refers to the Georgia Property Owners' Bill of Rights Act. State lawmakers passed the measure in April to create formal ways to resolve disputes between property owners and neighborhood associations. Sterling stressed that the case could have wider effects on property rights across Georgia. “This legislation represents an important step toward greater transparency and accountability, and I intend to pursue every legal remedy available to ensure Eva's rights are protected,” Sterling said in comments reported by Realtor.com. “This is about more than one homeowner,” he added. “It is about protecting the fundamental right to homeownership and ensuring that homeowners associations are not permitted to abuse their authority or use their power to harass and intimidate the very people they are supposed to serve.”Background and television historyMarcille first became widely known after winning America's Next Top Model. She later featured her search for the Alpharetta home during Season 12 of The Real Housewives of Atlanta. During the show, Marcille described the 0.3-acre property as her "forever home." The house includes a two-story main living room with a stone fireplace, a modern kitchen with built-in smart appliances, an outdoor back deck, and a sunroom. When Marcille bought the home in late 2019, she took sole ownership of the property and mortgage. She lives there with Sterling and her three children. Court records show that the homeowners association is seeking a financial judgment covering unpaid dues, accumulated late fees, daily fines for alleged violations, and legal costs linked to the lawsuit.You use AI every day. articles.title: KSEB seeks nod to procure power worth ₹336 crore
articles.summary: KSEB seeks KSERC approval to buy ₹336 crore power via DEEP portal for Oct 2026–Apr 2027, citing weak hydro inflows and a 1,200–1,500MW deficit.
articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: KSEB has sought Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (KSERC) approval to procure power worth Rs 336.246 crore through the Union ministry of power’s DEEP (discovery of efficient electricity price) e-bidding portal from Oct 2026 to Apr 2027. KSEB said deficient rainfall during southwest monsoon had resulted in poor inflows into major hydropower reservoirs, limiting the availability of hydroelectricity. At the same time, high temperatures had triggered a sharp rise in power demand, particularly during peak hours, widening the supply-demand gap.The board said its revised assessment indicated a power deficit of 1,200-1,500MW during March and April 2027. It therefore decided to procure power from various sources, including battery energy storage systems, thermal and pumped-storage projects. The procurement proposal covers early-morning and evening peak-hour blocks. Power has been tied up from companies including PTC India Ltd, Jindal Power Ltd, Tata Power Trading Company Ltd and Manikaran Power Ltd. The rates range from Rs 6.99/unit to Rs 13.89/unit, depending on the month and time block.The highest requirement is for 500 MW each during the midnight to 5am block in Oct 2026, Jan 2027 and Feb 2027 and 700 MW during the same block in Mar 2027. For April 2027, KSEB has proposed procurement of 550MW during the early-morning block and 600MW during the 6.30pm to 12 midnight slot.The board’s full-time directors had approved the procurement proposal at a meeting held on Sept 25. KSEB has now filed the petition under Regulation 78 of KSERC (Terms and Conditions for Determination of Tariff) Regulations, 2021, seeking the regulator’s approval.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: Leopard kills woman in Baglan, captured after 12-hour operation
articles.summary: Leopard kills 35-year-old woman in Baglan, Nashik; forest teams capture suspected male leopard after 12-hour search using cages, cameras and a drone.
articles.body: NASHIK: A 35-year-old woman was mauled to death and partially eaten by a leopard in Baglan taluka early on Tuesday morning. By nightfall the same day, forest officials tracked down, tranquillised and captured the animal suspected to be behind the attack after an intensive 12-hour search operation.The woman was attacked in the early hours of Tuesday when she was going towards a farm. The leopard pounced on her, dragged her towards a nearby nullah and fatally injured her throat and neck. Forest officials said the animal had partially fed on the body.The woman’s husband found the body during a search later in the morning and alerted authorities.The incident sparked panic in the village, where residents had reported repeated leopard sightings over the past few days. Villagers had also complained of attacks on domestic animals. The forest department had earlier installed three cages in the area to trap the animal.Following the fatal attack, forest officials launched a massive search operation. Eight cages and five trap cameras were deployed around the village, while a thermal drone was used to track the leopard’s movement.Officials said the operation began around 10 am as teams anticipated the animal would return to the spot where the attack took place. Surveillance continued through the day and into the night.After nearly 12 hours of tracking, the rescue team detected the leopard around 10 pm. The animal was darted, tranquillised and safely caged.“The captured animal is a male leopard, around two-and-a-half years old. Based on the evidence gathered and the territorial behaviour of leopards, we believe this is the animal involved in the attack,” a forest official said.The big cat was later shifted to the Transit Treatment Centre for wild animals at Mhasrul on the outskirts of Nashik for medical examination and further procedures.Forest officials have urged residents of forest-fringe villages to avoid venturing out alone during the night and early morning hours and to immediately report leopard sightings.ENDYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nashik | Silver Rate in Nashik | Bank Holidays in Nashik | Public Holidays in Nashik | Petrol Price in Nashik | Diesel Price in Nashik | CNG Price in Nashik | LPG Price in NashikStay updated with the latest Nashik news. articles.title: HC to CJP duo: You're not Gen Z; lawyer says they are an insporation
articles.summary: Delhi High Court questioned CJP co-convenors’ repeat peace-bond breach, said Article 226 plea improper, advised awaiting SEM hearing; duo later released.
articles.body: New Delhi: Before being released by the special executive magistrate (SEM) late Wednesday evening, Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka faced several questions in Delhi High Court earlier in the day.The duo had approached the court challenging the extension of their judicial custody by the SEM and later withdrew the plea after the high court advised them to await the outcome of the hearing scheduled before the special executive magistrate and approach the appellate court if their grievance continues.Justice Subramonium Prasad of the high court observed that a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution was not an appropriate remedy for a “repeat case” of violating a peace bond.During the brief hearing, Justice Prasad made oral observations, voicing his concerns over the conduct of the two CJP members.The high court pointed out that the petitioners had violated a bond by entering a denotified protest site, and questioned if the police weren’t entitled to seek a “stricter” surety in a “repeat case”.Justice Prasad said once the petitioners “have broken peace for the second time, are the authorities not entitled to insist upon everything?”The court wondered if it should enter into the merits of the SEM’s decision or let “the events run their course.”The judge remarked that the questions surrounding the locus and motive of the petitioners were also significant and have to be examined, considering that while they were initially involved in a student protest, there was even a statement on “regime change” and this time, their cause was different.“Now there is another cause. People remain the same, causes change. All these questions assume significance. When the issue is breach of peace, it is important to know who you are; what is your motive, what are you trying to do, the purpose of your organisation. You suddenly hear something like ‘regime change’..... In a hearing like this, it is not necessary for us to go into this. Keep the debate for an appropriate proceeding,” the judge said.The counsel for the petitioners, advocate Abhik Chimni, sought the high court’s immediate intervention and argued that they ought to be released on a personal bond as the SEM has no jurisdiction to extend their judicial custody. He argued that the SEM’s insistence on a surety was not sustained in law.Justice Prasad told Chimni that “when there is apprehension of peace and tranquillity (being broken), all these questions will assume importance” and emphasised that the purpose behind police permission for a protest is not to stop anyone but prevent “unwanted persons” from joining a protest group and ensure that a peaceful agitation does not escalate into violence.“The two petitioners here are at the forefront. When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people violating the 163 (section on prohibitory order) are very bright. There might be persons who might not be in your control and who might do things. We have seen it happening outside our country. Students’ protests have now gone into arson, looting, burning,” the court said.The court sought to know the age of the petitioners and was informed that Das and Ranka were 27 and 31 years old, respectively. The court then remarked in a lighter vein, “That means you are not Gen Z.”“They are an inspiration,” their lawyer responded.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
